title: The Evening Brief: Market pullback Friday as whale flows shift onto exchanges
dek: Friday saw broad crypto declines and a reversal in exchange inflows after three weeks of accumulation pressure, though spot Bitcoin ETFs drew modest inflows on the day. Leverage positioning across major assets remains tilted long, with funding rates warm but stable.
author: GoCheckMyCrypto
key_fact: The week ending October 16 brought only $104 million onto exchanges after three prior weeks of sustained inflows exceeding $2.7 billion, signaling a potential shift in accumulation patterns as prices decline across the board.
bottom_line: Friday brought distributed weakness with Bitcoin down 0.61% on the day and spot Bitcoin ETF inflows cooling to $5.1 million, while the week's cumulative exchange inflows slowed to $104 million after three weeks of $2.7 billion in accumulated inflows. Long-side leverage remains elevated across OKX, with Bitcoin long-short ratio at 1.83 to 1 and XRP at 3.68 to 1, while funding rates held warm and stable.
body: Friday's tape showed distributed weakness across the market. Bitcoin down 0.61% over 24 hours, Ether down 0.85% over 24 hours, and Solana down 1.04% over 24 hours, with broader market cap declining 3.6% on the day to $2.76 trillion. Cardano led gainers among the largest coins at up 17.62% over thirty days, while STRK down 14.86% over 24 hours topped the losers. Fear and greed stood at 63, in the Greed range, and Bitcoin dominance held steady at 59.4%.

The most significant datapoint came from exchange flows: the desk's whale watch shows $4.22 million in volatile net value moving onto exchanges over the 24-hour window, driven by $24.43 million in Dogecoin flowing onto Binance and partially offset by $20.21 million in PEPE moving off Poloniex. However, the weekly view tells a different story. The week ending October 16 saw only $104 million move onto exchanges, a sharp deceleration from the three preceding weeks ending September 25, October 2, and October 9, which saw $493 million, $931 million, and $1.28 billion move onto exchanges respectively. This represents a marked slowdown in the sustained inflow pressure that has characterized the past month.

Spot Bitcoin ETF flows sent mixed signals. On the day, October 15, spot Bitcoin ETFs took in $5.1 million, but over the week through October 15 they saw net outflows of $124.9 million. Spot Ethereum ETFs followed the broader pullback, with net outflows of $60.3 million on October 15 and last five sessions showing net outflows of $306.5 million.

Leverage and positioning data from OKX show persistent long-side crowding. Bitcoin open interest stands at $2.49 billion with a long-short ratio of 1.83 to 1; Ether's open interest is $1.4 billion with a 2.26-to-1 long ratio; XRP's open interest is $84.6 million with a 3.68-to-1 ratio; and Dogecoin shows a 3.34-to-1 long ratio on $94.3 million open interest. Funding rates remain warm but measured: Bitcoin 8-hour funding at 0.01% and annualized at 11.0%, Ether at 0.0079% 8-hour and 8.6% annualized, and XRP at 0.01% 8-hour and 11.0% annualized. Liquidations across the 4-to-8-hour windows show balanced small-cap liquidation pressure: 100 events per asset with roughly $200-500 thousand per venue per major asset. Solana stands as an outlier with negative 8-hour funding at -0.0012% and -1.3% annualized, and over the 6-hour window saw $1.1 million in long liquidations against $292 thousand in shorts.

Stablecoin supply sits at $305.2 billion, up 0.76% over the month, suggesting dry powder remains available but not yet deployed. All major assets remain above their 200-day moving averages and retain golden crosses, though RSI readings remain depressed across the board: Bitcoin 47.0, Ether 38.5, Solana 38.5, and most others clustered 36-43, all below the 50 midpoint. MACD signals have turned negative across all major assets.
